title: Fractal Correlation Properties of Heart Rate Variability as a Biomarker for Intensity Distribution and Training Prescription in Endurance Exercise: An Update
population: Review of DFA a1 studies in elite, recreational and cardiac disease populations, artifact handling and field tools
findings: DFA a1 of 0.75 has been associated with the aerobic threshold in elite, recreational and cardiac disease populations (termed HRVT); DFA a1 of 0.5 may be associated with the anaerobic threshold.
Common artifact correction methods induce minimal bias in DFA a1 at artifact levels below 3%, and HRVT changes negligibly even at 6%.
Several websites and smartphone apps can track DFA a1 retrospectively or in real time.
DFA a1 combined with non-autonomic markers such as pace or power opens possibilities for athlete durability and fatigue identification.
limitations: Narrative update by the group that originated the method (possible author bias); cites mostly small laboratory studies; the 0.5 upper anchor is described as 'may be associated' and is contradicted for sustained running by Gronwald 2024.
implications: Reject RR windows with more than about 3% artifact beats before computing DFA a1 (6% is the most the review reports as tolerable for HRVT).
Treat the DFA a1 = 0.5 upper-threshold link as tentative; do not use it to prescribe sustained running.

verification.notes: Added by verifier. Crossref: Front Physiol 2022 vol 13, Rogers & Gronwald; Europe PMC PMID 35615679 abstract states the figures.
